## Added

`dossier` reports the drawing set's technical-economic indicators table
(ՏՏՑ) as a new top-level `indicators` block: the plot, footprint and green
area in m², each with the percentage the table prints beside it, and the
page it was read from. The footprint comes as the rows the table prints (one,
or the house's and the fence's); the all-storeys total and a built area that
includes the paving are told apart and left out. Letter-spaced CAD capitals
and the legacy font's «Թ»/«fճ» units are read. A field the table prints twice
differently, or that two sheets disagree on, is left out rather than chosen.
The block is additive: `facts` and `checks` are unchanged, and a caller that
does not read it sees no difference. Seven reviewed annotations gain it and
nothing else.

## Fixed

Text on a page whose box is not the plain `0 0 width height` of how it is
displayed is read in full again. Two filters bounded a page's characters by a
rectangle anchored at the origin in the displayed orientation, while pdfium
places the characters in the page's own user space.

- `structured` markdown dropped every character left of or below the origin on
  a page whose MediaBox is centred, as some CAD exports write it
  (`[-595 -421 595 421]`): about three quarters of the page, the sheet's
  technical-economic indicators table among it. The off-page filter added in
  0.18.0 tested `0..width` × `0..height`; it now tests the page's crop box
  (else its media box), which is already in the page's own frame. Spans were
  never affected.
- The plain text layer that `text`, `inspect` and `dossier` read was bounded by
  the same kind of rectangle, and in the DISPLAYED orientation. It truncated
  the centred pages above, and every portrait page turned landscape with
  `/Rotate 90` or `270`, the usual shape of an A3/A4 drawing sheet, lost the
  text beyond the landscape height. This predates 0.18. All three now read
  through one helper, `pdf_core::page::visible_text` (the visible page's text,
  sanitized), and `clippy.toml` forbids `PdfPageText::all` so a new caller
  cannot bring the truncation back.

- `structured` no longer reads a CAD sheet's frame as a table. When one
  merged cell — the drawing area — covers more than 60% of a ruled grid, the
  grid is the sheet's frame, and its text is read as text. Read as a table,
  the title block's lines cut the drawing area into rows no table has, and
  the merged-cell fill copied the block's address and note into each of
  them, up to 21 times a sheet; on a scan, the page border drawn in the
  pixels put the whole page's text into one table cell a second time. Across
  twenty permit submissions the markdown is 20% shorter (one
  drawing album by about half) and holds more of each page's words, not fewer.
  A frame whose drawing area is cut into small cells by the drawing's own
  lines is still read as a table. The text bench is unchanged.

Two dossier readings that only showed once those pages became readable are
fixed as well:

- A page that only NAMES the Cadastre Committee's documents no longer counts
  as an official page. A marker phrase («Կադաստրի կոմիտե», «Հատված
  կադաստրային քարտեզից», …) now votes `official` only on a page with none of
  the applicant's own marks: a `table_of_contents` or `application_form`
  label, or the architect's «հատակագիծ» in its text — the same absence
  `looks_like_extract` relies on. A contents page or a sheet list naming the
  certificate made the whole drawing album `official`, the reference every
  cross-page check compares the other pages against. This reaches the
  offline route too, where no vision pass labels a contents page.
- An album's place-and-date stamp set on the address line (`… 63/2 ՀՈՂԱՄԱՍ
  ԵՐԵՎԱՆ 2026`) is no longer read as part of the address. Its year made two
  copies of one address disagree on their numbers. The stamp is matched in
  both spellings of «Երևան», since `և` in capitals is the two letters `ԵՎ`.

Three more, which the rebuilt scorecard ledgers below exposed:

- A cadastral map listing its parcels' codes with single spaces between them
  lost every second code, the subject parcel's among them: the pattern used the
  space as its boundary and consumed it, so the next code had none. Boundaries
  are now checked around each match; a code inside a longer run of digits is
  still not read.
- A person named with the father's name between the given name and the surname
  took the father's name into the `person:` id, so one person became two graph
  nodes. The patronymic is skipped wherever the page prints it, and both orders
  give one id.
- «պարիսպ» drops its «ի» when inflected («Պարսպի մակերես», «պարսպով»), and
  those fence areas were not read. The stem «պարսպ-» is a fence context word as
  well.

Across the reviewed corpus, seven of the fourteen dossiers read more text. Pages
that were routed `none` or `vlm` for lack of a text layer are now
`embedded_text`, and the dossiers find more facts and checks: parcel and
footprint areas, certificate numbers, address and applicant. None lost a
reading, and no new check disagrees. Dossier 8's drawing album goes back from
`official` to `applicant`; the reviewed annotation had recorded the
table-of-contents misreading. Off the reviewed corpus, the same rule turns a
drawing album's sheet list («ԳԾԱԳՐԵՐԻ ԱՆՎԱՆԱՑԱՆԿ», which names the cadastral
map extract among its sheets) from `official` to `applicant` on the offline
route. The seven annotations are regenerated, and the text bench is unchanged
from 0.18.3.

## Scorecard

The fourteen ledgers' `facts` and `checks` had been seeded from the toolkit's
own output and never checked against the pages. They are rebuilt from the page
images. Every page was read twice, independently: once auditing each ledger
entry and listing what the ledger lacked, once blind. An entry is kept,
corrected, removed or added only where both readings agree, and two independent
judges decided the rest on the image. About 23 wrong values are corrected and
about 263 missing facts added. A cadastral code counts only where it is printed
in full, and an address only where two readings agree on its key; page trust
follows the issuer, and the checks are recomputed by the toolkit's own rules.

Against these ledgers, facts score 0.7391 (0.18.3: 0.6388) and checks 0.7312
(0.18.3: 0.6773), and no dossier scores lower than on 0.18.3 in any kind. The
baseline is re-anchored on them, so its numbers are lower than 0.18.3's, which
were measured against the seeded ledgers. A ledger value now changes only when
the page shows it wrong or a new field or rule arrives, never to make a test
pass.
